0.5.n: Names the acting part she played.

0.6.n: Marks 役 as what she performed.

0.7.n: 演じる becomes 演じさせて, followed by humble いただきました, politely expressing gratitude for the opportunity.

0.10.n: つぐ belongs to the name つぐは; the subtitle has split the name into two pieces.

0.11.n: Here は completes the name つぐは; it is not the topic particle.

1.5.n: Adds friendly respect to the character’s name, even though the character is fictional.

1.6.n: Marks the character as the topic she will describe.

1.7.n: In はですね, this adds politeness while she pauses before the main description.

1.8.n: Gently draws the listener in as she introduces her explanation.

1.10.n: Combines with 自身 to emphasize her personal experience.

1.11.n: Emphasizes 私: she is talking specifically about her own acting experience.

1.12.n: Describes this kind of role as something she had not attempted before.

1.13.n: Links 初挑戦 to the later noun キャラクター, describing the character as a first-time challenge.

1.15.n: Describes a calm, reserved personality rather than simply an absence of sound.

1.16.n: Connects 物静か to the next description; this is the linking form of だ.

1.18.n: An emphatic, conversational version of すごい, used here to strengthen ミステリアス.

1.19.n: A borrowed adjective describing the character’s aura.

1.20.n: Connects the adjective ミステリアス to the noun 雰囲気.

1.21.n: Refers to the overall impression the character gives.

1.22.n: Links 雰囲気 to キャラクター, describing the character by their aura.

1.23.n: Refers to the fictional person she portrays.

1.24.n: The linking form of だ keeps the sentence open for her next comment.

2.0.n: Refers to the acting part offered to her.

2.1.n: Marks 役 as what she received.

2.2.n: Past form of いただく, a humble way to say she received something from someone.

2.3.n: The preceding phrase 役をいただいた tells us which moment she means.

2.5.n: Softens her assessment of how challenging the role might be.

2.6.n: Describes the role’s possible difficulty without specifying exactly what would be challenging.

2.7.n: Short for かもしれない, expressing uncertainty in casual speech.

2.8.n: Adds a reflective, talking-to-herself feeling inside her quoted thought.

2.10.n: Casually marks the preceding words as the thought reported by 思ってた.

2.11.n: Shortened from 思っていた, describing what she was thinking at that time.

2.12.n: Short for の, presenting her earlier thought as background to what comes next.

2.13.n: Adds politeness to the explanatory ん construction.

2.14.n: Leaves the sentence open, signaling a contrast with her initial concern.

0.lit: I had the privilege of playing the role of ???; I am Tsuguha!
0.tip: させていただきました humbly presents playing the role as an opportunity she was given.

1.lit: As for ???, you see, a first challenge for myself, a quiet character with a really mysterious aura, and…
1.tip: The final で connects this character description to the next part rather than ending the sentence.

2.lit: When I received the role, I was thinking, a bit difficult maybe, I wonder, but…
2.tip: って marks her inner thought, while 思ってた is the conversational shortening of 思っていた.
